Subject: Request: Reservation throughput validation & fallback plan

Vanessa,

Thanks for the materials so far — StellarDev is close to finalizing an RFP decision and we need a concise, technical response to a few items before procurement can sign off. Can you please provide the following by EOD Thursday?

1) Detailed SKU mix you recommend for a committed pool supporting 1.2M tokens/day at 95th-percentile P95 tail budget of 350ms for short-text generation workloads (average prompt + gen length = 64 tokens). Include per-SKU sustained throughput (req/s) and latency assumptions.
2) Define the acceptance test plan (what we run, pass/fail criteria, duration) you propose for validating on-commit throughput and tail latency.
3) Describe your SKU fallback policy if a primary GPU family (e.g., H100) is constrained — what compatible SKU families do you route to, how does that affect throughput/latency, and what additional cost or token pricing applies during fallback?
4) Burst policy: what burst capacity (headroom %) and slotting behavior do you allow for committed pools? Any constraints for warm-up or KV-cache priming?

We referenced your public docs but need explicit numbers that can be included in the SOW. If you can attach any concise worksheets or a slotting diagram that captures the proposed pool, that would be ideal.

Cheers,
Alex
Procurement Lead, StellarDev

Alex — thank you. High-level response below and we've attached a short workbook (redwood_throughput_matrix.xlsx) with per-SKU throughput numbers and the slotting diagram. Ben and Kim are looped in for the technical acceptance plan and fallback specifics.

Summary answers (short):
- Recommended committed SKU mix: predominately A100-80GB for cost-effective steady throughput + small H100 pool for low-latency burst lanes. Concrete numbers and runbook in the attachment.
- Acceptance tests: a 4-hour soak with staged QPS ramps and a 30-minute P95 measurement window at peak sustained load; acceptance when P95 < 350ms and error rate < 0.1%.
- Fallback policy: automated routing to compatible lower-latency families (A100 -> A100x or H100 -> A100) with explicit throughput degradation factors; token pricing applies per SKU on fallback (see sheet).
- Burst policy: committed pools get a baseline + 25% soft-burst allowance with 2x short-duration (5min) burst lanes subject to queueing; KV-cache warm-up expected ~1–2 minutes depending on prefix reuse.

I'll leave the technical detail to Ben and Kim, but happy to sync on a short call after you review.

Alex / Vanessa — adding the technical breakdown and explicit acceptance steps below. I also attached a compact throughput worksheet within the spreadsheet.

Assumptions (workload):
- Model family: Llama2.1-like; gen profile: prompt 16 tokens, gen 48 tokens average => 64 tokens total.
- Tokenization and batching: continuous batching up to 8 requests per GPU for short-text; KV cache warm when sessions reused.

Per-SKU sustained numbers (single-GPU, measured on typical Redstone benchmark):
- A100-80GB (fp16 / quant-friendly): ~180 req/s sustained (64-token avg), median latency ~90ms, P95 ~220ms under steady load.
- H100-80GB (optimized kernels): ~260 req/s sustained, median ~65ms, P95 ~160ms.
- A10/T4 class (inference tier fallback): ~45 req/s sustained, median ~350ms, P95 ~620ms (suitable only for non-latency-critical workloads).

Recommended committed pool for 1.2M tokens/day (rough calc):
- 1.2M tokens/day ≈ 18,750 requests/day at 64 tokens/request => ~0.22 req/s average. But peak/steady patterns matter — we size to peak sustained throughput of 250 req/s to cover burst windows and acceptance SLAs.
- Suggested mix for predictable SLA: 6 x H100 + 4 x A100-80GB (effective sustained capacity ~6*260 + 4*180 ≈ 2280 req/s raw; headroom, packing, and multi-tenancy reduce effective by ~60% => ~1368 req/s usable, which exceeds the 250 req/s target and provides runway).

Acceptance test plan (detailed):
1) Pre-test checklist: deploy target model version, pre-load KV caches with synthetic session traces, calibrate tokenization.
2) Soak test: 4-hour run; ramp 0 -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% target qps over 30-minute steps. Hold at 100% for 90 minutes.
3) Peak measurement: during last 30 minutes measure P95 latency, CPU/GPU util, and error rate.
4) Pass criteria: P95 latency < 350ms, error rate < 0.1%, throughput within +/- 10% of target sustained qps.
5) Fallback simulation: during soak, artificially remove 25% of H100 nodes to validate routing/fallback to A100 and confirm degraded but acceptable performance.

Fallback routing & effects:
- Policy: region-aware automatic fallback; prefer same-family fallbacks (H100 -> A100-80GB) before heterogenous fallbacks (A100 -> A10-class).
- Degradation factors: expect ~25–35% throughput drop when falling H100->A100, and ~7-8x drop when going to A10/T4 class. Communicated in the workbook with per-SKU multipliers.
- Pricing: fallback uses per-SKU billing rates (the invoice will reflect the SKU actually executed). For committed pools we include a protection corridor where short bursts on fallback are absorbed by the committed spend; prolonged fallback for >72 hours triggers a concession review.

Burst policy specifics:
- Soft burst: committed pools get +25% QPS for short windows (<= 5min) without additional charge; sustained bursts beyond 15 minutes are billed at on-demand SKU rates for the extra capacity.
- Warm-up: KV-cache hit-rate recovers within ~1–3 mins for steady sessions; use synthetic priming to reduce cold-start tails in acceptance tests.

I'll sync with infra if you want the exact kernel/cpu affinity map for the slotting diagram.

- Ben
